Claim 11 (currently amended): A method for training a molecular properties model on a computing system, comprising: obtaining a pseudo-partial ordering of molecules using a processing unit, wherein the pseudo partial ordering includes at least a representation of a first and second molecule, ordered relative to one another and a property of interest; and generating, using at least one processor, a representation of the molecules included in the pseudo partial ordering of molecules that is appropriate for a selected machine learning algorithm, wherein the pseudo partial ordering of molecules is provided to the selected machine learning algorithm, and wherein executing the selected machine learning algorithm on said computing system, using the pseudo partial ordering, trains a molecular properties model configured to generate a prediction regarding additional molecules supplied to the model.

Claim 12 (currently amended): The method of claim 11, wherein the molecular properties model generates predictions related to a property of interest selected from at least one of a pharmacokinetic property, pharmacodynamic property, physiological or pharmacological activity, toxicity or selectivity; a chemical property including reactivity, binding affinity, pKa, or a property of a specific atom or bond in a molecule; or a physical property including melting point, solubility, a membrane permeability, and a force-field parameter.

Claim 13 (currently amended): The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm comprises a classification learning algorithm executed on a computing device.

Claim 15 (currently amended): The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm comprises a variant of a Boosting algorithm, RankBoost algorithm, Alternating Decision Trees algorithm, Support Vector Machines algorithm, a Perceptron algorithm, Winnow, a Hedge Algorithm, decision trees, neural networks, genetic algorithms, genetic programming or any modifications thereof modified to process the pseudo partial ordering of ranked pairs via a computational processing means.

Claim 17 (currently amended): The method of claim 11, wherein the selected machine learning algorithm is configured to minimize, either directly or indirectly, a function of the rank ordering of molecules in the pseudo partial ordering executed on a computer.

Claim 19 (currently amended): The method of claim 11, wherein generating the representation of the molecules included in the pseudo partial ordering of molecules comprises: generating a vector representation of the molecules using a processing unit, wherein the vector representation is configured to encode the structure of the molecules included in the pseudo-partial ordering; or comprises generating an n-point pharmacophore representation of the molecules included in the pseudo-partial ordering using computational means.

Claim 21 (currently amended): The method of claim 11, wherein the at least one additional molecule comprises two or more additional molecules, and wherein the prediction comprises a ranked ordering of the two or more additional molecules, relative to one another and to the property of interest produced on a computing device.

Claim 22 (currently amended): The method of claim 11, wherein at least two of the molecules in the training set are alternative representations of the same physical molecule processed on a computational device and the property of interest is a property of the alternative representations.

Claim 23 (currently amended): The method of claim 11, wherein at least two of the molecules in the training set are encoded to represent different atoms, bonds, or substituent groups of the same molecule, and the property of interest is a property of said atoms, bonds or substituent groups determined using computer processing. 

Claim 35 (currently amended): A non-transitory computer-storage medium containing a program which, when executed by a processor, performs a method for training a molecular properties model, comprising: receiving a pseudo-partial ordering of molecules via a computing system, wherein the pseudo partial ordering includes at least a representation of a first and second molecule, ordered relative to one another and a property of interest; and generating a representation of the molecules included in the pseudo partial ordering of molecules that is appropriate for a selected machine learning algorithm executed on a processor, wherein the pseudo partial ordering of molecules is provided to the selected machine learning algorithm, and wherein executing the selected machine learning algorithm, using the pseudo partial ordering, trains a molecular properties model configured to generate a prediction regarding additional molecules supplied to the model.
